title: Deep Space Chroma · dispersion fields

reference.grammar: a cyclic dispersion fringe (black → crimson → orange → warm white → ice blue → steel → black) read along a phase field around a focus; sector occluders; heavy gaussian defocus; fine mono grain; lifted warm black
reference.set: 21 plates, 5000 × 3500, ø co. “Deep Space Chroma” key visuals

units: normalized by width: x ∈ [0,1], y ∈ [0, H/W]; angles in degrees, screen space (y down)

techniques.name: Cyclic dispersion ramp

params.cycle: no floor inside the cycle — the dark part is deep crimson/dusk; true black comes only from the envelope (wedges, pinch, vignette)

techniques.implementation: A 256-entry LUT built from the stops; phase = frac(a) indexes it, so a full lobe is one cycle: dark lane, red flank, white core, blue flank, dark lane. The red side spans .46 of the cycle and the blue side .30, which is why orange dominates.

techniques.name: Phase field · angle around a focus

params.ribbon: a = d / period, d = signed distance to y = cy + amp · sin(2π(freq · x + ph))

techniques.implementation: The only thing that differs between the 21 plates is this scalar field; the LUT and envelope are shared. Each structure family is one expression for a.

techniques.name: Unequal lobes
techniques.implementation: Two low harmonics of the angle stretch some lobes and compress others before the phase is taken, so no two lanes have the same width — the reference’s hand-made look without breaking the cycle count.

techniques.name: Pinch at the focus

params.note: plates 04, 09, 14, 16, 18, 19, 20 all pinch to a dark point

techniques.implementation: The envelope falls to the floor inside a small radius, so every lobe converges on a black point rather than a bright one.

techniques.name: Sector occluders

params.wedge: env *= smoothstep(hw − f, hw + f, |Δθ|) per occluder
params.other_plates: 08 = a cross of two wedges; 16 = a rectangle at the focus

techniques.implementation: Black wedges are multiplied into the envelope as gaussians of angular distance; they make the dark sectors that give the bursts their asymmetry.

techniques.name: Post-LUT gaussian defocus

params.measured: p99 horizontal gradient 12/255 per px at 1600 px; no edge sharper than ≈ 1 % of width
params.order: after the LUT, so colors mix in RGB and produce the grey-mauve between orange and blue

techniques.implementation: One blur over the finished color image. Blurring after the LUT (not the phase) is what makes neighboring lanes bleed into muddy transitions instead of clean fringes.

techniques.name: Mono grain

params.measured: black-region std 5.3/255; high-pass std 3.9/255; R/G/B high-pass correlation .96 / .95

techniques.implementation: Multiplicative hashed noise, identical across channels, so the grain reads as film rather than color noise.

techniques.name: Lifted floor + vignette

params.measured: reference L p10 = .048 (≈ 12/255); a mid-dark region reads (29,28,26)

techniques.implementation: Every pixel is mix(floor, LUT(phase), env): nothing reaches 0, and the far field sinks toward the floor with the square of the distance from the focus.

techniques.name: Phase flow (motion)
techniques.implementation: Sliding the phase moves the fringe through the lobes — the light crawls along each ray — while a slow rotation and warp drift keep the structure alive without changing it.

techniques.name: Structure families

params.presets: engine.html carries a first-pass preset for all 21

techniques.implementation: Each plate is a preset: one family, a focus or a curve, k, warp, twist, occluders. The engine reproduces any of them from ≈ 12 numbers.

pass_order: field · phase a(x,y) for the structure family
notes: LUT stops were fitted to per-luminance band means over all 21 plates; the white core is set to the brightest measured (222,190,184) rather than the mean.
Reference 09: focus at (0.47, 0.345 W), ≈ 9 lobes, two black wedges (up, σ 14°; down-right, σ 9°), blue lanes dominant on the left.
Fidelity is measured on the still at t = 0; the motion version is the same field with the phase sliding.
engine.html in this folder is the production system: the same math as a WebGL fragment shader, 21 presets, drag-to-focus, export.
